forswear

for-SWAIR · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To forswear is to solemnly promise to give up or reject something.

After the accident, the retired race car driver forswore ever getting behind the wheel again.

Worked Example

Following the corruption scandal, the mayor stood before the cameras and forswore all future donations from the construction industry.

Making a solemn public promise to give something up entirely is exactly what forswear means.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

swear off: Swear off is the everyday version of the promise -- you can swear off candy or late nights in one casual sentence. To forswear something is graver: a solemn, formal renunciation, often public and meant to be permanent.

relinquish: To relinquish something is to actually hand it over or let it go -- control, a title, a claim. To forswear is to promise: you solemnly vow to give a thing up, whether or not anything changes hands that day.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

embrace: to accept eagerly

resume: to begin again after stopping

Where it sits · how formally binding the rejection is — renounce → forswear → abjure

renounce vs. forswear: Renounce is milder than forswear: renouncing a membership publicly gives it up, while forswearing goes further, binding that rejection with a solemn promise never to return to it.

abjure vs. forswear: Abjure is more absolute than forswear: forswearing solemnly promises to give something up, while abjuring rejects it formally under oath, as a spy abjures all allegiance to his country.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — for-

prefix — for-: away; against; completely (Old English)

root — swear

root — swear: to make a solemn promise (Old English)

Put it together

Put it together: Forswear comes from Old English forswerian, combining the intensifying prefix for- ('away, against') with swerian, 'to swear.' To forswear something is literally to swear it away -- to reject it with the force of a solemn vow.

Use the root in a new word: swore

Use the root in a new word: swore: She swore she would never reveal the secret, no matter what.

Word Choice

Forswear is a formal, almost ceremonial word -- it's rarely used for small everyday decisions. Reserve it for a solemn, public, or deeply personal renunciation, not just 'deciding not to' do something.
